title.narrative: WASH intervention targeting IDPs and host communities

description.narrative: IDPs that have fled to Boulsa and families hosting IDPs

The objective of this project is to improve the WASH situation of the IDPs and their host families in the commune of Boulsa, Burkina Faso, building latrines and boreholes, rehabilitation WASH facilities and distributing hygiene kits, WASH kits, and establish and train committees to manage the function of the facilities.

The security and humanitarian situation continues to deteriorate in Namentenga province and in particular in the commune of Boulsa, provincial capital, with a number of Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) still growing. People have fled to Boulsa from Belga, Tangui, Poli Mossi, Poli Peulh, Tangui, Zaongo, Zaabga, Fatenga. There are more than 7,000 households, or approximately 52,311 individuals in Boulsa where people are now sheltering in public spaces and with host families, that in many cases is adding to the existing vulnerabilities of these households. This situation exacerbates the risks of prevalence of communicable diseases and Gender based violence. Due to the deterioration of the security situation in the surrounding localities, the displaced people are not expected to return to their villages anytime soon. Overcrowding is a serious problem and the WASH situation is concerning. Boreholes need to be rehabilitated and newly built because at the moment these facilities are inadequate in view of the new influx of populations in the city. Moreover, there is a need for more latrines for both IDPs and host families.
